FixedSplit.op_Division — three FusedArithmetic.AddProducts sums and two DivideProductSum restoring divisions over a SIGNED denominator
Legs.Against: Oracles.SplitQuotient → Oracles.RoundDyadicRatio: the exact BigInteger numerators (uc−vd, vc−ud) over the exact INDEFINITE form c² − d², one ties-to-even rounding at shift 16, wrapped. The sign of the quotient is the sign of the rational, which is precisely the statement the signed DivideProductSum overload makes and the definite complex case never reaches. ENVELOPE: there is no narrow fast path here — unlike op_Multiply, Norm and Transform, every operand takes the full-width branch, so this case carries no gate at all, which is a performance asymmetry rather than a correctness one

Legs.Subject: FixedSplit.FromRapidity over the twelve-row rapidity ladder — zero, ln 2, quarter/half/unit/one-and-a-half/double/triple/quadruple rapidity, and three negative mirrors
Legs.Against: Subjects.SplitRapidityLadder, a constant expectation table of raws with a per-row tolerance
Legs.Citation: hand-derived from the real hyperbolic cosine and sine of the value each RAPIDITY RAW denotes. The per-row tolerance is derived, not fitted: an argument error of at most 0.462·|φ| + 0.5 raws (the Log2E quantization plus the product's rounding) is a relative error of ln2/2¹⁶ per raw in the exponential, plus Exp2's own bound at these magnitudes — half a ULP from its closing narrowing and a relative term that is negligible this far below 2²⁰, 0.51 ULP per term — rounded up to a power of two; the halving is folded into the exponent (2^(s−1) + 2^(−s−1)), so no halving rounding exists and the sum is exact. Sharing no code and no substrate with the subject

Legs.Subject: FromRapidity(Zero) == MultiplicativeIdentity BIT-FOR-BIT: Exp2(−1) is exactly one half on both pre-halved calls — Exp2 is documented exact at whole exponents — so one half + one half is One and one half − one half is Zero with no rounding anywhere

the ln 2 row is the ladder's anchor and needs no analysis to read: cosh(ln 2) is exactly 5/4 and sinh(ln 2) exactly 3/4, both representable on the Q16 grid, and Exp2 is documented exact at whole exponents
the sign contract: V is zero or carries the sign of the rapidity, and U is positive, at every ladder row — so a swapped cosh/sinh wiring fails on sign alone before any tolerance is consulted
the Norm of each ladder row
Legs.Against: the constant One together with the row's own derived norm tolerance
Legs.Citation: cosh² − sinh² = 1 identically over the reals; the tolerance is 2·|U|·(the row's tolerance)/2¹⁶ rounded up, because quantizing cosh and sinh alone already moves the norm — which is why it is derived per row rather than shared

Legs.Subject: FixedSplit.FromRapidity over the six-row saturation ladder — the recovered representable band at rapidity 33, exact ±MaxValue saturation at 34 and its mirror, the first raw an un-widened wrapping scale once sign-flipped (6393185575658021189), and both carrier extremes; the norm identity is deliberately not consulted past the point where the backward exponential rounds to zero
Legs.Against: Subjects.SplitRapiditySaturationLadder, a constant expectation table of raws with a per-row tolerance
Legs.Citation: hand-derived at 200-bit precision for the rapidity-33 row (cosh and sinh round to the same raw, 7033440822424897606) with the T3 tolerance derivation at φ = 33 rounded up to 2⁵¹; the saturation rows are exact because past a scaled exponent of 48 the pre-halved terms are pinned to MaxValue and Zero with no rounding left. RULED: an un-widened wrapping scale answered a negative sine — or an all-zero pair — for every rapidity past raw 6393185575658021188, and halving after the sum capped the pair at 2⁴⁶, half the saturated value, while discarding the representable band up to rapidity ~33.27

Legs.Subject: the scaled exponent is formed at Int128 width — where raw × RawLog2E cannot wrap — and clamped to ±48 before narrowing, beyond the point where both pre-halved terms are constant, so the clamp changes no answer and no rapidity can flip the product's sign; the sum is exact because a term can only approach MaxValue once the other has rounded to Zero

the light-cone boundary the member's doc quotes: raw 726821 is still a unit off the cone, raw 726822 is the first exact U == V collision — the backward exponential 2^(−s−1) rounds to Zero once s exceeds 16, φ > 16·ln 2 ≈ 11.0904 — the negative mirror lands on the opposite diagonal, division by the collided pair is refused, and the collided pair times its own conjugate is the zero element
